video_title: Winners and Losers of the Offseason (With Brian Windhorst)

quotes.speaker: Brian Windhorst
quotes.summary_phrase: Lakers' acquisition of Walker Kessler was a necessary move
quotes.excerpt: pulling Walker Kessler when they needed that center so bad and I didn't see a clean path
quotes.quote: Pulling Walker Kessler when they needed that center so bad and I didn't see a clean path to get it. I did not think the Jazz were going to let Kessler go and the Lakers got it. They needed a player like that and they pulled him. You cannot ignore that. Absolutely excellent job to get him.

quotes.speaker: Brian Windhorst
quotes.summary_phrase: Mavericks lack perimeter defense with Luka Doncic as their best defender
quotes.excerpt: their biggest perimeter defender is Luka Doncic and he's not a good defender

text_blocks.speaker: Brian Windhorst
text_blocks.text: What I am worried about for them is they still don't have any big perimeter defense. Their biggest perimeter defender is Luka Doncic and he's not a good defender.

text_blocks.speaker: Brian Windhorst
text_blocks.text: No, but that's what I was saying. He's paired next to Jrue Holiday so it's just you don't even have a good defending backcourt.

quotes.speaker: Brian Windhorst
quotes.summary_phrase: Josh Grimes lacks the positional size needed for a big wing
quotes.excerpt: Grimes who they brought in is not a big wing. He doesn't have positional size
quotes.quote: Grimes who they brought in is not a big wing. He has good size relative to me, he is taller than me, but he is not taller than you, Shumpert. You are a big wing. They need a player or frankly, they need two guys.

quotes.speaker: Brian Windhorst
quotes.summary_phrase: Pistons missed opportunity to add perimeter help for Cade Cunningham
quotes.excerpt: they need someone to help Cade a little bit
quotes.quote: At midseason last year, we were like, man, the Pistons are good but they're missing that. They need someone to help Cade a little bit. They had all these expiring contracts that they could have and they owned all their draft picks. So they seem like, I remember when the Pistons won the last championship, Pistons had a really good team, but the piece that they needed right at the end was they traded for Rasheed Wallace and put him next to Ben Wallace.

quotes.speaker: Brian Windhorst
quotes.summary_phrase: Pistons' offseason moves fail to address their glaring needs
quotes.excerpt: they didn't do a move that affected their glaring need
quotes.quote: Their move was to trade for Isaiah Joe, who is definitely a shooter, but he's a backup. They resigned Kevin Huerter, which, okay, you're signing a shooter, that's what you want, but Landry Shamet got six million dollars a year, Kevin Huerter got nine million. Why don't you just go sign Landry Shamet for nine million? They literally signed them on the same day with like in an hour. Huerter, nine million, Shamet, six million. Shamet shot 10% more on threes last year than Huerter did. And then they let Tobias Harris walk. Tobias goes for 15 a year to San Antonio. That hurts losing him. They signed John Collins, it's a three-year contract, but really it's a one-year contract, only one-year guaranteed, so you're already admitting that it's a stopgap. I'm worried about them not maxing out this group.

quotes.speaker: Brian Windhorst
quotes.summary_phrase: Heat maximized their trade assets in the Giannis Antetokounmpo situation
quotes.excerpt: the way they handled this Giannis situation, they made the best of it
quotes.quote: The way they handled this Giannis situation, they made the best of it because they had Boston and Miami bidding against each other in the end and Miami put so much stuff in that trade that Milwaukee, obviously they would have gotten more for Giannis if they traded him two years ago, but the situation they were in, they maximized their situation. It's not even so much that the players that Miami sent were transformational players. I honestly think that Jaime Jaquez would be the best player ever in history of Giannis's career next to him. But because it cost so much, the picks and the swaps and all those players, that it depleted what Miami has, not only what they can put on the court, but also what they can trade for other pieces.

quotes.speaker: Brian Windhorst
quotes.summary_phrase: LeBron James remains the best available free agent

quotes.speaker: Brian Windhorst
quotes.summary_phrase: LeBron James's continued high-level performance and leadership
quotes.excerpt: he will carry your team emotionally, spiritually, set the agenda for your team
quotes.quote: LeBron averaged 22, 6 and 7 on 51% shooting last year. Not to mention, he can absolutely carry your team. He can play five if you need him to. He doesn't want to play it for long, but he can play five. He can play one. He will completely be the leader of your team. He will carry your team emotionally, spiritually, set the agenda for your team. Can you imagine getting him at four million dollars?

quotes.speaker: Brian Windhorst
quotes.summary_phrase: Jonathan Kuminga's development is hindered by his role
quotes.excerpt: he has long sort of felt that his role should be bigger than it has been
quotes.quote: The other guy I would say is Kuminga. He's a bit of a complicated player because he's a super athlete who can do a lot of different things, but he has long sort of felt that his role should be bigger than it has been on some of the teams he's on. I'm not saying he's wrong, but we've now seen two teams in the last year sort of just say, good luck to you, man. In terms of athlete and skill level for the money, I think he's probably up there too.

quotes.speaker: Iman Shumpert
quotes.summary_phrase: Victor Oladipo's persistent free agency status
quotes.excerpt: I saw Victor Oladipo post that he is still a free agent
quotes.quote: I saw Victor Oladipo post that he is still a free agent. Even though they keep bouncing him around, every time he does pop up, he does his thing. I wonder how much basketball he has left.
